conventions.convention: Work in four spacetime dimensions with c = ℏ = 1. The supplied fixed-weight complex quotient has dimension N ≥ 1; its ordered representatives all have engineering weight d. Coefficients are dimensionless in the formal expression Σ C_i O_i / Λ^(d−4). No reality condition or exhaustive physical interpretation of the relations is assumed.
The renormalization scale μ and cutoff Λ are distinct. With μ₀ ∈ J, t = log(μ/μ₀) is dimensionless and ranges over an open interval containing zero.

Realification lists real and imaginary parts alternately and is an isometry for Euclidean norms. Coefficients are column vectors; a supplied complex-linear flow uses C′ = Γ(t)C with this sign and matrix convention.

The ODE theorem assumes a continuous beta field on an open domain, with state-Lipschitz bounds locally uniform in scale. Its compact cylinders use a closed time interval times a closed Euclidean ball. The conclusion is local and supplies no global existence or omitted-term bound.
Scheme coordinate maps and beta fields are independently supplied data; a scheme record does not assert that its coordinate maps satisfy the supplied RG equation.

load_bearing.statement: A supplied finite-dimensional truncated RG datum consists of an open set Ω ⊂ I × R^(2N) and a continuous map β: Ω → R^(2N). A truncated RG trajectory is a continuously differentiable complex coefficient curve whose realification satisfies x′(t) = β(t,x(t)) and whose graph lies in Ω. The finite quotient, scheme maps, and vector field are supplied inputs; no QFT beta function or omitted-term bound is calculated.

For a supplied continuous beta field on an open RG domain, locally Lipschitz in coefficient coordinates locally uniformly in logarithmic scale, every (t₀,x₀) admits r,h > 0 and finite L ≥ 0 such that all initial states y,z ∈ B(x₀,r) have unique solutions on [t₀−h,t₀+h], with graphs in the domain, satisfying ‖x_y(t)−x_z(t)‖₂ ≤ exp(L|t−t₀|)‖y−z‖₂. Solutions through identical initial data agree on every common interval containing t₀.

published_dependencies.used_for: Defines finite-dimensional IVPs and interval solutions, including domain-relative endpoint derivatives.
Supplies the same-time state-Lipschitz inequality with one finite constant on each compact cylinder; the assigned theorem explicitly specifies its product-cylinder convention.
Converts the supplied ODE into its oriented integral equation on both sides of the initial scale, enabling the continuous-dependence estimate.
Supplies quantitative compact-cylinder local existence and uniqueness and agreement on common intervals. The assigned proof applies it uniformly to balls centered at nearby initial states.
Transitive operator-space prerequisite defining the complex reductive-group and unipotent-subgroup conventions used by the supplied finite-jet operator definition.

seams_checked.note: The scheme definition consumes only a supplied finite-dimensional fixed-weight complex quotient and ordered basis representatives. This matches the operator-quotient interface and preserves its restriction to explicitly declared relations, without asserting physical exhaustiveness.

The matching definition preserves the realification, dimensionless logarithmic-scale convention, and supplied-data status. The matching theorem cites common-interval uniqueness faithfully and separately assumes existence on the entire compact interval; it does not infer global existence or RG compatibility from the local theorem.

The QED example uses the distinction between renormalization scale and cutoff and the dimensionless scale logarithm faithfully. Its log(μ²/μ_*²) variable is explicitly defined, preserving the factor of two relative to t = log(μ/μ₀). The beta coefficients remain separately identified one-loop inputs.
